recent_posts.title: Training an AI chicken to run using reinforcement learning
recent_posts.summary: A developer showcases an AI locomotion project using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) instead of the NEAT evolutionary algorithm. The video documents training progressively complex bipedal structures, culminating in an AI-powered chicken model that learns to run at nearly 10 km/h. Key improvements include a graphical editor for building structures, tuning joint range of motion, and adding synchronization penalties to reward functions. The training process is shown iteratively, with the agent developing increasingly natural and fluid gaits over time.

recent_posts.title: Switching from evolutionary algorithms to PPO for AI locomotion simulation
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares progress on an AI locomotion project inspired by attending Nvidia's GTC conference. The post covers building a graphical editor for physical model assembly, fixing mass/density issues, and most importantly switching from evolutionary algorithms to PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) reinforcement learning using the MLAC C++ library. The comparison between the two approaches is striking: evolutionary methods plateau quickly and produce inelegant 'vibrating' solutions, while PPO produces smooth, physically convincing locomotion after about 30 minutes of training. The project uses a pogo-stick-like structure with collider constraints to force proper balancing behavior.

recent_posts.title: Ant Simulator 2 - Multiple Colonies
recent_posts.summary: A devlog update on an ant colony simulator covering several new features: an automated UI layout system replacing manual element placement, an ant life cycle with energy depletion and death, colony resource pooling for spawning new ants, and support for multiple simultaneous colonies. The multi-colony system uses a per-grid-cell colony ID approach instead of separate marker maps, removing the previous 4-colony cap. Colonies compete indirectly by overwriting each other's pheromone trails rather than direct combat. Several demo scenarios are shown with 2 and 4 colonies competing over food sources with and without terrain obstacles.

recent_posts.title: Building a cache friendly entity container with stable IDs
recent_posts.summary: A custom data structure combining vectors and indirection layers solves the entity storage problem in simulations. By using three vectors (data, data_index, and ID), it achieves fast iteration through cache-friendly contiguous storage, stable entity IDs through indirection, and efficient deletion via swap-and-pop. Benchmarks show vectors are 20x faster than lists for iteration due to cache locality, despite lists having better theoretical deletion performance. The solution maintains vector-speed iteration while providing stable identifiers and O(1) deletion.

recent_posts.title: How I create my UIs - 2, an example
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of building a custom time tracker application from scratch, demonstrating an iterative UI design process. The tutorial covers layout fundamentals using rounded rectangles, adding depth with shadows, implementing smooth hover animations through interpolated variables, creating parallel edges for nested elements, and building interactive timelines with tooltips. The design philosophy emphasizes intuitive user experience, consistent spacing, trial-and-error refinement, and minimalist aesthetics.

recent_posts.title: Using Evolution and Neural Networks to optimize Sailboat Races
recent_posts.summary: A project demonstrates using evolutionary algorithms and small neural networks to optimize sailboat racing routes. Starting with simple scenarios, boats learn to navigate checkpoints by adjusting angular velocity. The system evolves from basic navigation to handling wind effects using polar diagrams, with networks growing from single connections to compact multi-neuron controllers. Over 500 iterations, boats reduce completion time from 891 to under 650 seconds while maintaining surprisingly compact neural architectures. The trained agents show some generalization capability when tested on different race courses.

recent_posts.title: Ant Simulator 2 - Path Optimization
recent_posts.summary: Explores dynamic path optimization in an ant colony simulator when obstacles are added or removed during runtime. Implements two key improvements: blocked ants degrading obsolete trail markers to help colonies adapt faster to new obstacles, and introducing explorer ants (10% of population) alongside followers to discover better routes when shortcuts become available. Demonstrates how these mechanisms help ant colonies escape local minima and adapt to environmental changes, reducing harvest time from 65 to 26 minutes in obstacle scenarios. Also covers rendering improvements including shadow implementation using multiply blend modes.

recent_posts.title: Ant Simulator 2 - Ants vs Maze
recent_posts.summary: A detailed walkthrough of building an ant colony simulator with improved navigation algorithms, obstacle handling, and pathfinding optimization. The implementation includes a custom UI system, marker-based navigation with exponential decay, collision detection optimization, and exploration strategies that help ants navigate complex mazes. Performance tests demonstrate how the colony adapts to different obstacle configurations, with ants collectively finding near-optimal paths through tunnels and around barriers.

top_posts.title: AI Cat Learning to Run
top_posts.summary: A developer creates AI agents that learn to walk using neural networks and evolutionary algorithms. The project simulates cat-like creatures with virtual muscles and joints, using Box2D physics engine for stability. Through iterative training with 1,000 agents running in parallel across 14 CPU cores, the AI gradually develops from basic movement to smooth walking gaits. The training process shows how agents evolve from struggling with joint coordination to achieving efficient locomotion patterns over 240+ iterations.

top_posts.title: Ant Simulator 2 - Bigger Simulation
top_posts.summary: Ant Simulator 2 introduces new features including multi-threading for realistic ant collision behavior and improved animation systems inspired by real ant movements. The project also addresses and resolves previous marker system issues by implementing exponential decay, enhancing the reliability of ant path-finding. Further development plans involve adding obstacles to explore more complex interactions.
